quote: Fortune, we go forth to reign; / Wake me not if this is vision, / Let me sleep not if ’tis true. / But whichever of them is it, / To act right is what imports me.
source: Pedro Calderón de la Barca, Life Is a Dream, Act III, scene IV, the close of the scene (Sigismund) (trans. Denis Florence MacCarthy, 1873)
speaker: Sigismund

evidence.where: Project Gutenberg eBook 6363, a transcription of the 1873 volume, read in full at the passage
evidence.edition: Calderon’s Dramas: Life Is a Dream, trans. Denis Florence MacCarthy (London: Henry S. King and Co., 1873)
evidence.locator: Act the Third, Scene IV, Sigismund's speech after Clotaldo's exit, before the stage direction Exeunt all, drums beating

reason: Read verbatim in MacCarthy's 1873 translation at Act III, scene IV, with the edition's lineation and a full stop after imports me. The only change is the straight apostrophe in ’tis curled. The Spanish obrar bien es lo que importa is the play's most cited resolution.
